note: CP-1 recruits of Port Marlin. Fields mirror the crew_member schema (id, name, age, gender male, role, stats, loyalty_start) so module D can promote them to real crew records; cost and effect are CP-1 economy values (provisional, owner B4/D2). Text placeholders: {cost} {have} {missing}. The Canon content rules apply to every line.

crew_pip_larkin.name: Pip Larkin
crew_pip_larkin.place: the signal mast on the plaza

effect.text: Calls the shoals from the masthead: +10% fish in every haul.

crew_pip_larkin.speech_style: Quick, eager, runs sentences together, calls everyone Cap'n, counts things aloud.
crew_pip_larkin.backstory: A rope-maker's son who learned to read the sea from the harbour signal mast. His spyglass was his father's.
crew_pip_larkin.notice: WANTED, a ship: lad with a good eye and a spyglass, at the signal mast. Pip Larkin, asks 18 dollars.
pages: Cap'n! You're the one with the sloop at the end of the pier, aren't you? I've been watching your sloop come in all week.
I can see a gannet dive from this mast at two miles. Put me up your mainmast and I'll call every shoal before the nets are wet.
I'm asking eighteen dollars, paid once, and I'm yours. I want a ship under me, not a fortune.
crew_pip_larkin.offer: Eighteen dollars, and I sign today. Will you take me on, Captain?
crew_pip_larkin.poor: Eighteen dollars, Cap'n, and you've {have}. Sell me a net of fish first: the market is west along Quay Street, past the bridge. I'm not going anywhere.
crew_pip_larkin.accepted: Aye aye, Captain! I'll be aboard before you've cast off. Mind my spyglass: it was my father's.
crew_pip_larkin.declined: Right. I'll be up the mast, then. Just here. Waiting.
crew_pip_larkin.aboard: Pip is aboard, up at the masthead.

crew_tuck_marrow.name: Tomas "Tuck" Marrow
crew_tuck_marrow.place: the net frames on the west wharf

effect.text: Mends and works the nets: +25% fish in every haul.

crew_tuck_marrow.speech_style: Dry, short sentences, calls the player skipper, never wastes a word he can mend a net with.
crew_tuck_marrow.backstory: Mends nets on the west wharf for a fish-merchant who pays him in promises.
crew_tuck_marrow.notice: NET-HAND for hire, west wharf. Tuck Marrow asks 30 dollars on the nail.
pages: Mind the needle, skipper. This net has more holes than a tax collector's promise.
Ten years on this wharf, hauling for a man who pays in promises. Give me a good net aboard and your catch grows by a quarter.
Thirty dollars and I'll sign. I don't work for promises. I work for pay on the nail.
crew_tuck_marrow.offer: Thirty dollars for a net-hand who never drops the haul. Hire him?
crew_tuck_marrow.poor: Thirty, skipper. You have {have}. Come back with {missing} more and I'll have the net ready.
crew_tuck_marrow.accepted: Done. I'll bring my own needle. Don't touch the knots.
crew_tuck_marrow.declined: Suit yourself, skipper. The net won't mend itself, so I'll be here.
crew_tuck_marrow.aboard: Tuck is aboard, working the nets.

crew_silas_reed.name: Silas Reed
crew_silas_reed.place: the well in the Fish Row market yard

effect.text: Salts and packs the catch in cold brine: fish spoils 30% slower.

crew_silas_reed.speech_style: Proud, a little pompous, speaks of food as other men speak of battles.
crew_silas_reed.backstory: Cooked for three tavern keepers, every one of whom let him go for improving the recipes.
crew_silas_reed.notice: COOK seeks a galley, by the well in the market yard. Silas Reed asks 40 dollars and a clean pot.
pages: Do not look at the stew, Captain. Look at me. I am the man who has been improving it.
A crew that eats badly fights badly. And fish, left in a hold in the sun, is a crime. With salt and cold brine I keep a catch sweet a third longer.
Forty dollars, a clean pot and no remarks about my seasoning. That is all I ask.
crew_silas_reed.offer: Forty dollars for a cook who keeps your catch sweet. Take him aboard?
crew_silas_reed.poor: Forty dollars, Captain. You have {have}: that is {missing} short. Fish, sell, and return. A great kitchen is not built in a day, but a great purse might be.
crew_silas_reed.accepted: Splendid! I shall bring my own salt. And my own pot. And my opinions.
crew_silas_reed.declined: A pity. The soup will mourn. I will be here when you are hungry.
crew_silas_reed.aboard: Silas is aboard, already arranging the galley.

crew_garrick_stave.name: Garrick Stave

effect.text: Builds drying racks and a second fish-hold: the hold carries 20 kg more.

crew_garrick_stave.speech_style: Gruff and slow, measures everything twice, says little and means all of it.
crew_garrick_stave.backstory: Built hulls in the Anvil yard for thirty years until the yard closed. Still keeps his adze sharp.
crew_garrick_stave.notice: CARPENTER, boatyard behind the warehouses. Garrick Stave asks 55 dollars. Bring tools.
pages: Don't lean on that. I measured it.
Thirty years building hulls in the yard until it closed. Your sloop is sound, but the hold carries fish like a basket carries water.
Give me a week of planks and I'll add a second hold, twenty kilos more. Fifty-five dollars. Measure twice, pay once.
crew_garrick_stave.offer: Fifty-five dollars for a carpenter who adds twenty kilos to the hold. Sign him?
crew_garrick_stave.poor: Fifty-five. You've {have}. I don't build on credit: wood costs.
crew_garrick_stave.accepted: Good. I'll bring the adze. Don't let anyone near the planks.
crew_garrick_stave.declined: Hm. The planks will keep. So will I.
crew_garrick_stave.aboard: Garrick is aboard, measuring the hold.
